To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the liver is a systemic hub for the whole-body metabolism and detoxification, that oxidative stress occurs in all cellular compartments and that it is the basis for liver diseases.
Oxidative stress in the liver is not only a consequence of liver injury but it is also the main cause of liver injury.

(i) oxidative stress is not a single event, but a complex phenomenon, which involves the disruption of the organelle's redox homeostatic circuits and (ii) the hepatocyte is a model for the study of the redox state in the healthy and in the wounded liver.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of redox signaling and the mechanisms of oxidative stress in normal and wounded cells.
understanding the mechanisms of oxidative stress in liver diseases.

the role of oxidative stress in liver diseases and in particular with the mechanisms by which hepatocytes respond to oxidative stress and the role of oxidative signaling in hepatocyte function and survival.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
oxidative stress occurs in all cellular compartments, in the healthy and injured hepatocytes, and that it is a key player in liver homeostasis.
the hepatocyte redox balance is maintained by an intricate and dynamic network of prooxidant and antioxidant molecules and that the hepatocyte is a master regulator of the systemic redox balance.
the hepatocyte redox state is a key determinant in the development of liver injury and regeneration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hepatocyte's cellular organelles red ox homeostasis is a key factor that determines liver health and disease.
the redox balance is a fundamental determinant of the hepatocyte homeostasis and its disruption is a hallmark of liver disease.
the hepatocyte is a highly specialized cell with a complex redox network, which is tightly regulated and integrated with other cellular processes to maintain the redox balance.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the redox state is a dynamic parameter, which is not only a consequence of the balance between the pro- and anti-oxidative systems but is also actively regulated to fulfill the specific functions of the cell compartments.
the redox state is a key determinant of the cell's response to injury.
the hepatocyte's redox state is tightly controlled at the organelle level and that oxidative stress is a key component of the wound-healing cascade.
